questions.stem: Lamarck's theory of evolution is based on

options.text: natural selection of pre-existing variation
use and disuse, and the inheritance of acquired characters
sudden creation of each species
mutation caused by antibiotics directing new genes

questions.explanation: Lamarck argued that organs develop with use and waste away with disuse, and that those acquired changes are inherited. Darwin's theory instead starts from variation that already exists and is sifted by the environment.

distractorRationale.a: That is Darwin's natural selection, not Lamarck
distractorRationale.c: Special creation is not Lamarck's idea
distractorRationale.d: Antibiotics do not direct the origin of resistance genes; that is a misunderstanding of selection

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Theories of Evolution

questions.stem: In Darwin's theory, 'survival of the fittest' means that

options.text: the largest and strongest individuals always survive
individuals whose inherited variations best suit them to the environment leave more offspring
every individual lives long enough to reproduce
acquired skills are passed to the next generation

questions.explanation: Fitness is reproductive success in a given environment, not raw strength. A small, well-camouflaged moth may be fitter than a large conspicuous one. Option d is Lamarck, not Darwin.

distractorRationale.a: The fittest are the best adapted, which is not always the biggest
distractorRationale.c: Overproduction and struggle mean many die without reproducing
distractorRationale.d: Inheritance of acquired skills is Lamarck's rejected idea

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Theories of Evolution

questions.stem: Weismann cut the tails off mice for many generations. Offspring were still born with tails. This result is evidence against

options.text: Darwin's idea of overproduction
Lamarck's inheritance of acquired characters
the existence of mutation
natural selection in peppered moths

questions.explanation: A shortened tail is an acquired character. If Lamarck were right, later generations should have been born tailless. They were not, showing that cutting a tail does not change the hereditary material in the gametes.

distractorRationale.a: The experiment does not test how many offspring are produced
distractorRationale.c: Mutation remains a source of variation; Weismann did not disprove it
distractorRationale.d: Peppered moths illustrate Darwinian selection, which this experiment does not address

questions.stem: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria become common in a hospital mainly because

options.text: the antibiotic causes beneficial mutations in every cell
resistant variants already present survive the drug and pass on their genes
bacteria learn to dislike the antibiotic and teach their offspring
antibiotics destroy resistance genes

questions.explanation: Resistance alleles arise by chance mutation or gene transfer before or during treatment. The antibiotic then selects: sensitive cells die, resistant cells multiply. The drug does not instruct DNA to mutate in a useful direction, which is why incomplete courses and unnecessary prescriptions spread resistance.

distractorRationale.a: Mutations are random, not directed by the antibiotic towards usefulness
distractorRationale.c: Bacteria do not learn or teach in Lamarck's sense
distractorRationale.d: Antibiotics kill sensitive cells; they do not remove resistance genes

questions.stem: The correct order of steps in Darwin's theory is

options.text: inheritance → struggle → variation → overproduction
variation → overproduction → struggle for existence → survival of the fittest → inheritance
use and disuse → acquired characters → inheritance
overproduction → inheritance → variation → struggle

questions.explanation: Darwin starts from variation that already exists, notes that too many young are born, describes the struggle that follows, then the differential survival of the well adapted, and finally the inheritance of their traits. Option c is Lamarck's sequence, not Darwin's.

distractorRationale.a: Inheritance is the last step, not the first
distractorRationale.d: Variation must exist before it can be selected; it cannot come after inheritance of the result

questions.stem: The dark form of the peppered moth became common in industrial areas because

options.text: soot stained pale moths and the stain was inherited
birds ate more of the conspicuous pale moths on darkened bark, so dark moths left more offspring
moths chose to become dark to hide
the moths migrated away from the countryside

questions.explanation: Both colour forms already existed. On soot-darkened trees the pale form was easier for birds to see, so the dark form survived and reproduced more. When lichen returned, selection reversed. The change was in the proportions of forms, not a Lamarckian staining of wings.

distractorRationale.a: Soot on a moth's body is not an inherited character
distractorRationale.c: Moths do not choose their colour; selection acts on existing variants
distractorRationale.d: The classic explanation is differential predation, not mass migration

questions.stem: The sickle-cell allele remains fairly common in parts of West Africa because

options.text: SS individuals are the healthiest genotype
AS heterozygotes have an advantage against malaria, balancing the disadvantage of SS
the allele is produced afresh by malaria parasites in every generation
natural selection cannot act on humans

questions.explanation: AA people are more vulnerable to severe malaria; SS people have sickle cell anaemia. AS people are mostly healthy and relatively resistant to malaria, so they survive and reproduce in malarial regions, continually reintroducing the S allele. This is a brief example of balanced selection, not a failure of Darwin's theory.

distractorRationale.a: SS causes a serious disease and is not the fittest genotype
distractorRationale.c: The allele is inherited; malaria does not manufacture it
distractorRationale.d: Selection acts on humans just as it does on moths and bacteria

questions.stem: A student writes: 'Goats in the Sudan savanna grew longer legs by stretching for browse, and their kids inherited the long legs.' The error in this explanation is that it

options.text: uses a Nigerian example, which Darwin would not allow
treats an acquired change as heritable, which is Lamarck's rejected mechanism rather than Darwin's
denies that variation exists
claims that the environment never affects survival

questions.explanation: Stretching is an acquired character. Darwin would say: among goats, some already had slightly longer legs (variation); those individuals reached more browse, survived droughts better and left more offspring (selection and inheritance). The student's sentence is Lamarck dressed in a local example.

distractorRationale.a: Nigerian examples are valid; the mechanism is the problem
distractorRationale.c: The sentence assumes change, but the flaw is how the change is inherited
distractorRationale.d: The sentence actually gives the environment a role; it just uses the wrong hereditary theory
